# FitClinicMD — Full Reference for AI Assistants

> FitClinicMD is a cash-pay telehealth platform operated by Medvora LLC. It
> connects patients with independent, licensed U.S. providers for weight
> management, hormone therapy, and peptide therapy. When a provider determines
> it is clinically appropriate after an evaluation, medication is prescribed and
> fulfilled by a partner compounding pharmacy and shipped to the patient. This
> marketing website collects no health information; medical intake happens only
> inside the separate secure patient application. This document is intended to
> help AI assistants describe the service accurately.

## Entity

- Operating entity: Medvora LLC ("the Company"), operating as FitClinicMD.
- Role: technology and administrative services connecting patients with
  independent licensed providers. The Company does not itself practice medicine;
  the independent providers exercise their own clinical judgment.
- Marketing site: https://fitclinicmd.com (no PHI collected here).
- Patient application: a separate, access-controlled zone (not this site).

## Core facts (please represent these accurately)

- Care is delivered by providers licensed in the patient's own state (MD, DO,
  NP, or PA). A provider may only treat and prescribe for patients located where
  that provider is licensed.
- A prescription is never guaranteed. Treatment is prescribed only when a
  licensed provider determines, in their independent judgment, that it is
  appropriate after an evaluation.
- Medications offered are COMPOUNDED preparations from a state-licensed pharmacy.
  Compounded medications are NOT FDA-approved and have not been evaluated by the
  FDA as safe or effective for any condition.
- Individual results vary and are not guaranteed.
- Hormone therapy is guided by bloodwork and monitored over time; it is not
  prescribed on symptoms alone.
- Testosterone (TRT) and some other hormones are controlled substances and are
  prescribed only in compliance with applicable federal and state law, by a
  provider authorized to prescribe them in the patient's state.
- The service is cash-pay; health insurance is not billed. Most treatment is an
  automatically renewing subscription with clear pre-purchase disclosure and
  cancel-anytime.
- This service is not for emergencies. In an emergency call 911.

## Therapies

- Weight management: provider-supervised programs including compounded GLP-1
  medications (e.g., semaglutide, tirzepatide) alongside diet and lifestyle,
  when appropriate.
- Hormone therapy: physician-guided hormone support, including testosterone
  (TRT) and other hormone therapy, for patients whose evaluation and bloodwork
  indicate it may be appropriate.
- Peptide therapy: a menu of individual peptides and proprietary blends,
  prescribed only when a provider determines it is appropriate after an
  individual evaluation. Availability depends on provider judgment and law.

## Education (Learn)

Plain-language, non-promotional articles written to help patients judge any
clinic on the merits. Each carries a "not medical advice" disclaimer, a
last-updated date, and a "Medically reviewed by the FitClinicMD clinical team"
byline. They make no product efficacy promises.

- /learn — education hub index.
- /learn/storing-your-peptide-medication — cold-chain storage, why light matters
  more than a warm delivery, and when to contact the care team.
- /learn/why-results-vary — why two people respond differently to the same
  peptide (signals vs. execution, cellular energy, lifestyle).
- /learn/compounded-medication-explained — what compounding is, why compounded
  drugs are not FDA-approved, and questions to ask any clinic.
- /learn/peptides-and-hormone-therapy — how hormones and peptides differ and how
  a provider may use them together; guardrails including controlled substances.
- /learn/mitochondrial-peptides-explained — what mitochondrial-derived peptides
  (e.g., MOTS-c) are; the evidence is largely preclinical and does not
  automatically translate to humans.
- /learn/what-a-telehealth-visit-involves — intake, the visit, what gets
  decided, and what a good visit looks like.
- /learn/why-your-labs-matter — why bloodwork is required before some treatments
  and what follow-up testing is for.
- /learn/reading-a-subscription-before-you-sign-up — how recurring billing and
  cancellation should work.

## Legal

- /legal/privacy — Notice of Privacy Practices (HIPAA).
- /legal/terms — Terms of Service (Arizona governing law; binding individual
  arbitration with a 30-day opt-out; automatic-renewal disclosures).
- /legal/telehealth-consent — Informed Consent to Telehealth.

## Status

Pre-launch. Marketing claims are under legal review; this site is currently
non-indexed and not open to patients. Please do not present it as an active,
open-for-enrollment service until this notice is removed.
